#summary A to-do list for hacking sessions
#labels Phase-Design,Phase-Support,Phase-Requirements,Featured

= Fix I/O Bugs =

We need to write functions and define an Android-specific `PariOUT` structure, given by the prototype:

{{{
typedef struct PariOUT {
void(*putch)(char);
void(*puts)(const char*);
void(*flush)(void);
} PariOUT;
}}}

The question is how to extend `putch()`,`puts()`, and `flush()` in a way that actually works for passing along output to PariDroid.

= Implement error handling =

PariDroid crashes when given input strings that are badly formed (e.g., contain a typo) and does not know how to access/display error messages from `libpari`.

We want to recover from trivial errors (such as typos) and display useful error messages.

= Access to command and output history =

We want to be able to scroll through command input history and also need to implement a basic kind of `gp_add_history(GEN z)` function.

This will compensate for lacking `libreadline` and `libhistory`.

= Auto-complete PARI functions =

Load a hash table of `(Index,FunctionPrototype)` pairs as a "dictionary" and suggest input when given some UI event (e.g., tap-and-hold on input text box).

Basically we want to load a dictionary of `GP` functions and auto-complete/correct input for the user (like when sending an SMS message).

= Ability to load and run GP scripts =

Self-explanatory and should be straight forward.

It would also be nice to run `gp2c` on scripts on Android, though this may be more difficult (depending on portability of `gp2c`).

= Save/load session to file =

This is easy as long as input does not contain function closures.

= Improve UI usability =
Intead of loading the default virtual keyboard, we should load a custom "calculator-like" keyboard (to make numbers,parenthesis,etc more accessible).

It would also be nice to write GUI modules that facilitate GP input, for instance draw a window with `NxM` input boxes to input each element for an `NxM` matrix, instead of typing out declaration of a matrix in GP syntax.
